title: Businesses enjoy summer downtime before busy football season kicks off - NewsBreak
text: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. ( WIAT ) – SEC Media Days is helping to ramp up excitement for football season. With about a month and a half before football starts, fans are getting ready, and businesses are prepping for how busy it will be. “We’re just kind of enjoying the downtime,” Innisfree Irish Pub manager Chris Davis said. “We’re about a month away from busy season, so getting our staff in order, hiring some new people and just kind of laying out the game plan for August to get here.” Davis says away games can bring in more business than home games, but that doesn’t mean home games are slow. He says football season is great because there are so many people who come in from out of town, and they get a chance to show off what Tuscaloosa is all about. “When you get an SEC home game in town, you’re going to get teams that travel a lot better than a regular team would from out of town, so it’s a fun rivalry that comes into town, some fun trash talk, all that kind of stuff,” he said. “But in here, yeah it gets crazy. Especially when the game is on.” Innisfree Irish Pub is a staple for many Alabama fans during football season. some going so far as to line up hours before the doors are unlocked. “We open at 11, but people are here at 9 a.m. that day, getting ready, and a lot of those people don’t leave until 3 or 4 in the morning, so it’s grueling to say the least,” said Davis. Davis says bid day marks the start of busy season as it rolls right into football. He says game days at Innisfree are organized chaos. Right now, Davis says their football season prep looks like hiring and making sure they’re fully staffed and ready to go. “We have a lot of turnover, we have a lot of people who graduated this past May, so just getting them trained, kind of just getting them on the same page so everything runs smoothly on a busy game day like we tend to have,” Davis said. Elaina Poole is a server and bartender at Innisfree. She’s seen firsthand how crazy a game day can get. “Throughout the day, there’s consistently a line pretty much all the way around the corner,” Poole said. “Which is good for business and good for tips, so I don’t mind it. It can be a little overwhelming though when you’re just taking down chairs and you see the huge line of people.” Poole says the most popular drinks on game days are car bombs, grimace bombs and Saban-ades. But despite the sea of people from open to close, she says there’s moments of peace on game day. “Whenever a big play is happening or we’re about to score, you don’t have to do anything because everyone is looking at the TVs, which is kind of like very calming, and you get to watch it too,” she said. “But also, when Alabama wins, Dixieland Delight is played, and that’s the best part because you also don’t have to serve anyone, it’s just everyone singing and you’re finally enjoying like a moment of calmness.” Alabama’s first football game of the season is August 30 against Florida State University in Tallahassee. The Tide’s first home game of the season at Bryant Denny Stadium will be September 6 against the University of Louisiana Monroe.
